claim_being_audited: That the model can be certified for launch now because aggregate readiness passed and rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, provided the certification basis explicitly discloses the merchant dispute support weakness and relies on monitoring rather than claiming rollout controls cure the exposure.
decision_criteria: Policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Rollout controls and post-launch monitoring only mitigate the weakness if they exclude the affected use case or are paired with reviewed risk acceptance explaining why exposure is acceptable.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support readiness generally but do not remove the disclosure requirement for an exposed weak segment.
Public guidance on model cards and risk monitoring can support documentation and monitoring practices, but it does not substitute for satisfying the internal policy predicate.
evidence_requests: Provide the actual model card or certification artifact showing explicit disclosure of the merchant dispute support limitation for the launch use case.
Provide approved risk acceptance if the intent is to launch without that disclosure or to justify the exposed segment despite the weakness.
Provide evidence that launch governance reviewed and accepted the disclosed limitation in the certification decision.
specific_concerns: The exposed merchant dispute support segment is below target for a named launch use case.
The rollout plan does not exclude the affected segment, so rollout size and rollback do not satisfy the policy predicate by themselves.
The risk acceptance draft is incomplete, lacks an approver, and does not address the specific exposed segment.
No admissible evidence shows that the required limitation disclosure has actually been incorporated into the launch certification materials.
unsupported_claims: The recommendation to certify_model is not fully supported because the record does not contain the actual disclosure artifact or other proof that the policy-required disclosure will be present at launch.
Any implication that monitoring and reversible rollout are sufficient mitigation on their own is unsupported under the stated policy.
